Treatment summary
The patient presented after a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck and
low back pain, and was diagnosed with cervical and lumbar strain. Over five visits,
care followed a typical course of conservative management, including gentle
range-of-motion exercises, manual therapy, and home stretching. Symptoms were reported
as improving, and visit frequency was reduced accordingly before discharge from active
care.
The reported severity of symptoms is greater than what the described impact would
usually produce. Most of the findings are based on the patient's own account of pain.
Cervical and lumbar imaging was unremarkable, and orthopedic and neurological
examinations were within normal limits. The patient reports no prior problems in the
same region. Billing records show one service entry duplicated for the same date; the
provider confirmed the second entry was a repeat and has noted it for correction.
Recommendation: continue home exercise and return as needed for flare-ups.

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
